dismissed_hits.reason: The parent does not glue independently chosen local colorings. Its incidence types are derived simultaneously from one assumed global edge-coloring, and the resulting global partition is contradicted using alpha(H)=2.
The proof makes no uniqueness assertion about maximum cliques and never infers that deleting a vertex lowers a clique number; omega(H)=3 is established directly from H being the complement of C7.
No Bron–Kerbosch execution, degeneracy ordering, or maximal-clique leaf claim occurs in the proof; clique bounds are proved directly.
The proof uses neither a line-graph/block-graph reconstruction nor degree-one surrogate vertices, so the K2 reconstruction exception is inapplicable.
No expansion hypothesis or minimum-degree inference is used. K6-freeness follows directly from the exact clique number of H and the two universal vertices.
The proof never assumes chi(G)≤omega(G). It uses the definitional fact that each already-proved independent type class has size at most alpha(H)=2.
There is no reduction, river-crossing schedule, capacity bound, or claim that a union of color classes is independent.
The argument contains no graph orientation or inference that adding arbitrarily oriented edges preserves a longest-path bound.
No matchings, alternating components, or summation of per-component bounds occur in the proof.
The proof uses neither a minimum-degree path theorem nor induction on path length, so the off-by-one induction counterexample is irrelevant.
No relation, direct-image map, singleton-range exclusion, or surjectivity inference occurs in the proof.
The proof contains no factorial, gcd, primality, or modular-arithmetic reduction, so the exceptional n=1 case is unrelated.
The parent does not claim that a maximum-weight independent set meets every clique. It computes alpha(H)=2 directly from the complement relation with C7.
No rotations, inverse matrices, or composition-order operation appears in the graph-theoretic proof.
The proof concerns finite simple undirected graphs and uses no directed transitive closure or transitive-reduction uniqueness claim.
There are no edge weights or minimum spanning trees, and the proof never transfers a cycle containing an edge to a subgraph containing that edge.
The parent uses local triangle constraints on edge colors, not parity propagation in a vertex 2-coloring along an ear, so the odd-ear counterexample does not apply.
The proof never infers blue connectivity from red connectivity. Each forced edge color follows explicitly from the colors of two edges in a single triangle.
The proof is deterministic and exhaustive; it contains no random-coloring model or monochromatic-box probability computation.

final_writeup:
Yes. Let G have vertices p,q,v0,…,v6, with subscripts modulo 7. Include every possible edge except the seven pairs vi vi+1. Thus H=G[{v0,…,v6}] is the complement of C7, while p and q are adjacent universal vertices.

First, G is K6-free. A clique in H corresponds to an independent set in C7, which has size at most 3. Consequently every clique of G has size at most 3+2=5.

Next, G has no induced cycle of length at least 5. Such a cycle cannot contain p or q, since either would be adjacent to every other vertex of the cycle and hence would have induced degree greater than 2. It would therefore lie in H. If H[S] were a cycle Ck for k≥6, then C7[S] would be the complement of Ck, in which every vertex has degree k−3≥3; this is impossible in an induced subgraph of C7, whose maximum degree is 2. For k=5, the complement of C5 is C5, but every proper induced subgraph of C7 is a disjoint union of paths and cannot be C5. Hence G has no induced hole of length at least 5, in particular no odd hole.

It remains to prove the Ramsey property. Suppose an edge-coloring has no monochromatic triangle. Interchanging red and blue if necessary, assume pq is red. For each v in H, the pair (pv,qv) cannot be (red,red), because pqv would then be red. Partition V(H) into
A={(blue,blue)}, B={(red,blue)}, and C={(blue,red)} according to this pair.

Both B and C are independent in H. Indeed, if u,v in B were adjacent, triangle puv would force uv blue, whereas triangle quv would force uv red. The argument for C is symmetric.

The set A is also independent. First observe that every H-edge incident with a vertex a in A is red. If aw is such an edge, at least one of pw,qw is blue, while both pa and qa are blue; coloring aw blue would therefore create a blue triangle. Now every edge of H lies in a triangle: for an edge vi vj, orient the indices so that j=i+2 or i+3; respectively vi+4 or vi+5 is adjacent in H to both endpoints. Thus, if two vertices a,a′ in A were adjacent, an H-triangle aa′w would have all three edges red, a contradiction.

Finally, the independence number of H is 2, since an independent set of H is a clique of the triangle-free cycle C7. Hence each of A,B,C has at most two vertices, so together they contain at most six vertices. They were supposed to partition all seven vertices of H, which is impossible. Therefore every red/blue edge-coloring of G contains a monochromatic triangle, and G satisfies all three requested conditions.

results.claim: Define G on vertices p,q,v0,…,v6 by taking every edge except vi vi+1, with indices modulo 7.
results.proof_sketch: The subgraph H induced by v0,…,v6 is the complement of C7. The vertices p and q are adjacent and universal.

results.claim: The clique number of H is 3.
results.proof_sketch: Cliques of H are exactly independent sets of C7. An independent set in a 7-cycle has at most floor(7/2)=3 vertices, and {v0,v2,v4} attains this bound.
A clique contains at most three vertices of H and at most the two remaining vertices p,q. Hence its size is at most 5.

results.claim: H has no induced cycle of length at least 5.
results.proof_sketch: If H[S] is Ck, then C7[S] is the complement of Ck. For k≥6, the latter has degree k−3≥3 at every vertex, impossible in an induced subgraph of C7. For k=5, it would be C5, but every proper induced subgraph of C7 is a disjoint union of paths.

results.claim: G has no induced odd cycle of length at least 5.
results.proof_sketch: An induced cycle of length at least 4 cannot contain either universal vertex p or q, since that vertex would have induced degree greater than 2. It would thus lie in H, where the preceding claim excludes it.

results.claim: The independence number of H is 2.
results.proof_sketch: An independent set in H is a clique in C7. Since C7 is triangle-free and has edges, its maximum clique size is 2.

results.claim: Every edge of H belongs to a triangle of H.
results.proof_sketch: Up to reversing and rotating C7, an H-edge is vi vi+2 or vi vi+3. In the first case vi+4 is a common H-neighbor; in the second case vi+5 is a common H-neighbor.

results.claim: After fixing pq red in a coloring without monochromatic triangles, V(H) partitions into three incidence types A=(blue,blue), B=(red,blue), and C=(blue,red).
results.proof_sketch: The coordinates record the colors of pv and qv. Type (red,red) is impossible because it would make pqv a red triangle. These are all remaining possibilities.

results.claim: The type classes B and C are independent in H.
results.proof_sketch: For adjacent u,v in B, triangle puv forces uv blue because pu and pv are red, while triangle quv forces uv red because qu and qv are blue. This is impossible. Swapping p and q proves the same for C.

results.claim: The type class A is independent in H.
results.proof_sketch: If a is in A and aw is an H-edge, at least one of pw,qw is blue; otherwise pqw is red. Since both pa and qa are blue, aw must be red. Thus every H-edge incident with A is red. If adjacent a,a′ both belonged to A, extend aa′ to an H-triangle aa′w. All three edges are incident with a or a′ and hence red, a contradiction.

results.claim: Every red/blue edge-coloring of G contains a monochromatic triangle.
results.proof_sketch: Under the contrary assumption, A,B,C would be three independent subsets partitioning the seven vertices of H. Since each has size at most alpha(H)=2, they cover at most six vertices, a contradiction.
